note: Attacker-controlled bytes are written verbatim into the temporary input file.
The parser reads the first byte as the packet tag from the attacker input.
The tag selects new-format packet parsing for this crafted first byte.
The low bits make the packet type 12, which dispatches to the comment-packet handler.
The length byte is decoded as zero, so the comment packet has an empty body.
The code subtracts 1 from an unsigned length of 0, producing a huge allocation size and triggering the memory-safety bug when the parser allocates the comment packet.
